headline: Fermi, which is building a large power and AI data-centre site in the Texas Panhandle, signed a credit support deal with AMD, and its shares jumped 13.2% before the market opened.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: read in full; a company announcement with specific figures, but the share move is a premarket move and the 17 gigawatt scale depends on agreements not yet signed.
importance_line: What changed is that a chip maker is backing the first lease at a planned very large AI power and computing site, which matters first to the communities and power users around the Texas site, then to lenders deciding whether to finance it, then to Fermi and AMD, and the doubt is that the 17 gigawatt scale depends on customer agreements not yet signed and the share jump was a premarket move.
summary: Investing.com reports that Fermi Inc, developer of the Project Matador energy and AI infrastructure site in Carson County, Texas, announced a credit support agreement with chip maker AMD that backs the lease for the site's first phase of 222 megawatts, a key step toward securing financing, and that Fermi shares rose 13.2% in premarket trading on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026. The two companies also signed a framework agreement for a possible expansion of up to 650 megawatts, and the site could grow to about 17 gigawatts, but only if binding customer agreements follow; Fermi says it has invested more than $1.5 billion so far.
notes: Investing.com's report read in the Yahoo Finance copy; link is the Yahoo copy because the Investing.com page was not found. The lessee is not named.
